title: Review: Crystal Lake suffers a bit from its obsession with Pam Voorhees
gist: Ashley Belanger reviews Peacock's Crystal Lake, a prequel series to Friday the 13th from showrunner Brad Caleb Kane that builds a backstory for Pam Voorhees (Linda Cardellini) by shifting Jason's drowning to 1971-2 and adding a corporate experimentation plot. The review says early episodes feel slow and foreign to franchise fans, but by episode three the series turns to familiar camp slayings, re-created scenes and heavy practical gore.

themes.theme: Expanding Pam Voorhees beyond the original film

insights.claim: Betsy Palmer, who played Pam Voorhees in the 1980 Friday the 13th, refused to return in later films largely because the character had no depth and the sequels gave her only "stupid" lines; she took the original role for $10,000 for 10 days of work after her Mercedes broke down and she needed a new car.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Shows the long-standing unmet fan interest in Pam's character that the Peacock prequel is trying to monetize.
insights.quote: “I read that script and thought ‘What a piece of junk,’” Palmer said in 2005.

insights.claim: Belanger argues that Peacock's Crystal Lake, though slow and foreign for die-hard Friday the 13th fans in its first episodes, is worth sticking with as the first real attempt to make Pam Voorhees more than a helicopter mom to a vengeful son.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: A mixed-to-positive review signal for a franchise reboot on a streaming platform competing for horror audiences.
insights.locator: Palmer often criticized the later movies

insights.claim: Crystal Lake showrunner Brad Caleb Kane, who previously produced HBO's Welcome to Derry, moved Jason's drowning from 1958 in the original movie to 1971-2 so the story could draw on real experiments on mothers in the early 1960s and invent a corporate enemy whose experiments on Pam make her a mother who would kill for her son.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Franchise IP owners are willing to bend canon to fit prestige-drama formats, which Kane already did for IT's Pennywise.
insights.quote: he told the Daily Dead that he got to weave in a scientific “Douglas Sirk-meets-David Cronenberg” body horror episode

insights.claim: According to the review, Kane's added backstory raises the tension of Jason's drowning at the camp and makes Pam's belief that Jason is alive and needs her to kill counselors more relatable.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Character-driven expansion is the series' main selling point beyond slasher nostalgia.

insights.claim: Kane said that when he pitched Crystal Lake to A24 he wanted to do his own thing, but kept as sacred that some fans feel the show is a loving homage, so the series reuses town-folk names, lines and Pam's cable-knit sweater from the original movie.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: An example of the homage-plus-new-territory formula used to hold legacy fans while reaching new viewers.
insights.quote: “what was sacred to me is that a certain segment of the fans feel like I was doing a loving homage to the movies,”
insights.locator: When pitching the series to A24

insights.claim: In Crystal Lake, Jason begins to feature more prominently from the third episode, when gory deaths start and the series picks up pace. Kane re-creates exact scenes from the original movie, though the hockey mask never appears.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Episode-three payoff timing matters for retention on a streaming series.

insights.claim: Kane told Esquire he hopes Crystal Lake will be a hit so it can run for multiple seasons.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Whether the show is renewed is the key signal for Peacock's investment in the Friday the 13th IP.
